plan: Given my private value of $3, bidding aggressively is not profitable. I expect Betty and Charles to bid close to their values. If I bid above $3, I risk paying more than the prize's worth. To win and still maintain a profit, I should bid slightly above $20 but below my value. A bid of $21.5 could outbid opponents while keeping a potential profit margin.

Given my value of $11, I aim to bid below my value to avoid overpaying. Assuming Andy and Betty bid near their values, I’ll bid $10.9 to potentially win if their values are lower. This strategy maximizes profit by ensuring I pay less than my value if I win. If I bid higher and win, my profit decreases due to overbidding. If I bid lower and lose, I miss potential profit. Balancing the bid close to my value optimizes my chances of winning without overpaying.
